column1: # One line per repository: slug, the commit the corpus was taken at, the license GitHub reports for that
# repository, and the stratum the repository belongs to. The commit is pinned rather than a branch name so that
# `fetch.sh` reproduces the same file set on any later day; a repository that rewrites history will fail the fetch
# loudly instead of silently returning a different corpus.
# Selection: public repositories of systems that read or write Avro, chosen before any schema was looked at, and
# kept whether or not their schemas turned out to be interesting. Repositories with zero `.avsc` files at the pinned
# commit were dropped and are listed in `excluded.tsv` with their counts, so the selection is auditable. This is a
# convenience sample of open-source infrastructure, not a random sample of Avro schemas in the world, and the
# measurement reports that limit rather than hiding it.
# Stratum: `platform` is a system that processes other people's data, so its schemas are mostly its own internal
# records. `application` is a system whose schemas describe its own domain. The distinction matters because the two
# have different reasons to declare a field required, and the relevance measurement reports them separately.
